simple.meaning: שָׂתַר (sâthar) is a Hebrew action word meaning “to break out (as an eruption).” BibleIQ anchors the English reading to this source verb before comparing its uses.
simple.biblicalBackground: This action appears 1 time in 1 Samuel, beginning at 1 Samuel 5:9. The surrounding contexts include city.

definitions.full: H8368. sathar [ שָׂתַר ] verb Niph`al burst or break out , of tumours (Arabic have inverted , or cracked, eyelids , or lower lips ; Ethiopic lacerate ; Assyrian [ šatâru ] II. tear down ; Syriac destroy , so Sabean שתר SabDenkm No. 48, 1. 2 , Biblical Aramaic סְתַר Ezra 5:12 ); — Niph`al Imperfect עפלים לָהֶם וַיִּשָּֽׂתְרוּ 1Sam 5:9 and tumours brake out to them.

occurrences.englishText: It was so, that after they had carried it there, Yahweh’s hand was against the city with a very great confusion; and he struck the men of the city, both small and great, so that tumors broke out on them.
